questions.question: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, is also known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UMEED Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which is popularly referred to as the **UMEED Act**, was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **August 8, 2024**.
 
• The acronym **UMEED** stands for **Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development**. This name reflects the government's objective to modernize and streamline the administration of Waqf properties in **India**.
 
• The bill was introduced by **Kiren Rijiju**, the Union Minister of **Minority Affairs**, aiming to amend the existing **Waqf Act, 1995**, which had been criticized for lacking transparency and accountability.
 
• One of the primary **features** of the **UMEED Act** is the mandatory **registration** of all Waqf properties on a **centralized portal** to ensure better monitoring and prevent illegal encroachments.
 
• The act proposes significant changes to the composition of the **State Waqf Boards** and the **Central Waqf Council**, including the mandatory representation of **two women** and **two non-Muslim** members to ensure a more inclusive administrative structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context of Waqf Laws:**
 
 
• The first major legislation was the **Waqf Act, 1954**, which was later replaced by the more comprehensive **Waqf Act, 1995**.
 
• In **2013**, the **United Progressive Alliance (UPA)** government introduced amendments to provide more powers to the Waqf Boards, but the current **2024-2025** amendment seeks to balance these powers with **government oversight**.
 
 
 
• **Definition of Waqf:**
 
 
• **Waqf** refers to the permanent dedication of movable or immovable **property** for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
• The person making such a dedication is known as a **Wakif**, and the manager of the property is called a **Mutawalli**.
 
 
 
• **Central Waqf Council:**
 
 
• It is a **statutory body** established in **1964** by the **Government of India** under the original Act.
 
• Its **function** is to advise the Union Government on matters concerning the working of **State Waqf Boards** and the due administration of Waqf properties in the **country**.
 
 
 
• **Waqf-al-Aulad:**
 
 
• This refers to a **Waqf** created for the maintenance and support of the donor's own **family** and descendants. The **UMEED Act** seeks to bring more clarity to the rights of women in such family-based endowments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the District Collector:** Under the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, the power to conduct a **survey** of Waqf properties and decide whether a property is "Waqf" or "Government land" has been transferred from the **Survey Commissioner** to the **District Collector**.
 
• **Removal of 'Waqf by User':** The new bill proposes to remove the concept of **Waqf by User**, meaning a property cannot be declared as Waqf merely because it has been used for religious purposes for a long **duration**; it now requires a formal **Waqfnama** (deed).
 
• **Financial Audits:** To increase **efficiency** and reduce corruption, the act mandates that the **accounts** of Waqf Boards be audited by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** of India or a designated authority.
 
• **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):** Following intense debate in **Parliament**, the bill was referred to a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)** consisting of **31 members** (21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha) for further scrutiny and stakeholder consultation.
 
• **Data and Scale:** India has the largest **landholding** under Waqf outside the Islamic world, with over **8.7 lakh** registered properties covering approximately **9.4 lakh acres** of land across various **states**.
</ul

questions.question: Who became the first athlete in history to run sub-10 s in the 100 m for 11 consecutive years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Akani Simbine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **South African** sprinter **Akani Simbine** made history in **July 2024** by becoming the first athlete to record sub-10 second times in the **100m** for **11 consecutive years**.
 
• He achieved this milestone at the **London Diamond League** held at the **London Stadium**, where he clocked a season-best time of **9.86 seconds**.
 
• This remarkable streak began in **2014** when he first broke the **10-second barrier**, and he has maintained this world-class performance level every single year through **2024**.
 
• By reaching 11 consecutive years, he officially surpassed the previous record of **9 consecutive years** held by the legendary **Jamaican** sprinter **Usain Bolt**, who maintained his streak from **2008 to 2016**. ***Hence, the statement regarding his record-breaking consistency is correct.***
 
• The **Diamond League** performance in **2024** served as a crucial warm-up for the **Paris 2024 Olympics**, reinforcing his status as one of the most consistent sprinters in athletic history. ***Hence, Akani Simbine is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Akani Simbine:**
 
 
• Born on **21 September 1993** in **Johannesburg, South Africa**, Simbine is a specialist in the **100 meters** sprint.
 
• He is the **South African national record holder** in the 100m and has consistently finished in the top 5 at major championships, including the **Tokyo 2020** and **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
• His career is defined by extreme consistency, having reached the finals of the **World Athletics Championships** and **Olympic Games** multiple times since **2016**.
 
 
 
• **Usain Bolt:**
 
 
• An **eight-time Olympic gold medalist**, Bolt is the world record holder in the **100m (9.58s)** and **200m (19.19s)**.
 
• While he is considered the greatest sprinter of all time, his streak of sub-10 second finishes lasted **9 years**, ending with his retirement in **2017**.
 
 
 
• **Trayvon Bromell:**
 
 
• An **American** sprinter who was the first high school athlete to break the 10-second barrier.
 
• Although he has recorded extremely fast times, including a personal best of **9.76 seconds**, his career has been plagued by **Achilles tendon injuries**, preventing a long consecutive yearly streak.
 
 
 
• **Andre De Grasse:**
 
 
• A **Canadian** sprinter and the **2020 Olympic 200m champion**.
 
• Known as a "big-game performer," De Grasse has won numerous medals at the **Olympics** and **World Championships**, but his sub-10 second performances in the 100m have not occurred in **11 consecutive years**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **sub-10 second barrier** is a historical hallmark of elite sprinting. While many athletes have achieved it, maintaining the physical condition to do so annually for over a decade is rare due to the high risk of **injuries** and **age-related** physiological declines.
 
• **Asafa Powell**, another **Jamaican** legend, holds the record for the **most total sub-10 second clockings** in history (97 times), but Simbine’s record focuses on the **consecutive nature** of the years in which the feat was achieved.
 
• The **World Athletics** governing body tracks these statistics to highlight longevity in the sport, where **Akani Simbine** now stands as the benchmark for sustained excellence in the **100m dash**.
 
• Simbine's 2024 season also saw him anchor the **South African 4x100m relay team** to a **Silver Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**, further cementing his legacy in **African athletics**.

questions.question: Which telemedicine platform served over 36 crore patients by April 2025, per the Ministry of Health?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**eSanjeevani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **eSanjeevani** is the **National Telemedicine Service** of India, designed to provide online medical consultations to citizens across the **country**.
 
• By **April 2025**, the platform achieved a significant milestone by serving over **36 crore** patients, as reported by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**.
 
• It was conceptualized to implement **Ayushman Bharat**'s mandate of providing health and wellness services digitally, ensuring that **rural** and **remote areas** have access to quality healthcare.
 
• The platform operates through two primary modes: **eSanjeevaniAB-HWC** (provider-to-provider) and **eSanjeevaniOPD** (patient-to-doctor), facilitating a wide range of medical advice from **general medicine** to **specialized care**.
 
• This initiative has been instrumental in reducing the **out-of-pocket expenditure (OOPE)** for patients by eliminating the need for long-distance travel to reach **tertiary care hospitals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **eSanjeevaniAB-HWC:**
 
 
• This is a **doctor-to-doctor** telemedicine system launched in **November 2019**.
 
• It connects **Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs)** at the village level with **Hubs** located at **District Hospitals** or **Medical Colleges**.
 
• This model ensures that patients at the **grassroots level** can consult with **specialists** without leaving their locality.
 
 
 
• **eSanjeevaniOPD:**
 
 
• Launched during the **COVID-19 pandemic** in **April 2020**, this variant allows **patients** to consult doctors directly from their **homes** using a **smartphone** or **laptop**.
 
• It features **video consultations**, **online prescriptions**, and **SMS notifications**, making it a highly **user-friendly** application for the general public.
 
 
 
• **Technological Backbone:**
 
 
• The platform was developed by the **Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC)** in **Mohali**.
 
• It is integrated with the **Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)**, allowing for the seamless creation of **Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA)** IDs and the digital storage of **health records**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Impact:**
 
 
• States such as **Andhra Pradesh**, **Tamil Nadu**, **Karnataka**, and **Uttar Pradesh** have emerged as leaders in terms of the highest number of **teleconsultations** performed on the platform.
 
• The service supports over **20 languages**, making it accessible to a diverse population across different **geographical locations** in **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Data and Statistics:** The platform records an average of over **4 lakh** consultations daily, showcasing its **scalability** and the growing **digital literacy** among Indian citizens.
 
• **Specializations:** Beyond general consultations, the platform offers access to **super-specialty** services in areas like **Cardiology**, **Oncology**, and **Gynaecology** through its **hub-and-spoke** architecture.
 
• **Global Recognition:** **eSanjeevani** has been recognized globally as one of the **world's largest** government-run telemedicine taxonomies, serving as a model for **digital health** interventions in developing **nations**.
 
• **Inclusion:** The service is provided **free of cost** to all citizens, fulfilling the **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3** of ensuring **healthy lives** and promoting **well-being** for all at all **ages**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following cities hosted the National Workshop in July 2025, organised by the Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to strengthen the implementation of the SMILE-B (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise – Begging) scheme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Workshop** on the **SMILE-B** (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise – Begging) scheme was organized in **Indore**, **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• This workshop was conducted on **July 10, 2024** (notably the most significant recent national gathering for this scheme), by the **Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment**, **Government of India**.
 
• The primary objective of the workshop was to strengthen the implementation of the **SMILE-B** sub-scheme and facilitate the **rehabilitation** of persons engaged in the act of **begging**.
 
• **Indore** was selected as the host city due to its exemplary performance in social initiatives and its status as a leader in urban cleanliness and **social welfare** management.
 
• The event saw participation from more than **100 delegates**, including **Municipal Commissioners** and representatives from **30 pilot cities** across the **country**, along with officials from the **National Institute of Social Defence (NISD)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The SMILE Scheme:**
 
 
• Launched on **February 12, 2022**, the **SMILE** (Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise) scheme is a central sector umbrella initiative aimed at the welfare of marginalized groups.
 
• It encompasses two major sub-schemes: **SMILE-B**, which focuses on the **Comprehensive Rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of Begging**, and **SMILE-T**, focused on the welfare of **Transgender persons**.
 
• The **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment** has allocated a total budget of **Rs. 365 crore** for the implementation of this scheme for the **five-year** period from **2021-22** to **2025-26**.
 
 
 
• **Core Components of SMILE-B:**
 
 
• **Survey and Identification:** Identifying individuals engaged in begging through rigorous **field surveys** conducted by municipal authorities and **NGOs**.
 
• **Mobilization:** Encouraging individuals to move to **shelter homes** and access government services through persistent **counseling** and outreach.
 
• **Shelter and Resettlement:** Providing basic facilities like food, clothing, and safe living conditions in dedicated **rehabilitation centers**.
 
• **Education and Skill Development:** Offering vocational training and **skill-building** to ensure long-term **economic independence** and integration into mainstream society.
 
 
 
• **Implementing Agencies:**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented through **State Governments**, **Union Territory administrations**, **Local Urban Bodies**, and **Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)**.
 
• The **National Institute of Social Defence (NISD)** and **National Backward Classes Finance & Development Corporation (NBCFDC)** play pivotal roles in **capacity building** and financial support.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Pilot Cities Initiative:** Initially, **30 cities** across **India**, including **Delhi**, **Mumbai**, **Chennai**, **Kolkata**, **Bengaluru**, and **Hyderabad**, were selected to run **pilot projects** for the **rehabilitation** of persons in begging.
 
• **Convergence with Health Schemes:** Beneficiaries under the **SMILE-B** scheme are integrated with the **Ayushman Bharat** (Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana) to ensure they receive **comprehensive health insurance** and medical treatment.
 
• **Social Security and Dignity:** The scheme aligns with the spirit of **Article 21** of the **Constitution of India**, which guarantees the **Right to Life with Dignity**, by focusing on **rehabilitation** rather than criminalization.
 
• **Data Management:** A centralized **portal** has been developed to track the **progress** of beneficiaries and maintain a database for **transparency** in fund utilization and **impact assessment**.

questions.question: Which of the following banks launched the largest staff engagement initiative called ‘Next LEAP’ to empower workforce in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The State Bank of India (SBI) launched the ‘Next LEAP’ initiative in May 2025 as part of its massive workforce empowerment and staff engagement drive.
 
• Scale: It is the largest staff engagement and training programme ever undertaken in the Indian banking sector, targeting SBI's entire workforce of approximately 2.3 lakh employees.
 
• 'Next LEAP': Focuses on direct engagement between top management and employees to ensure skill adequacy and gather ground-level feedback.
 
• 'SuPer SBI: Great to Greater': A mass training program aimed at instilling organizational pride and equipping staff with future-ready skills.
 
• Objectives: The initiative aims to enhance productivity, operational efficiency, and customer service by fostering a growth mindset and leadership potential across all levels of the bank.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Profile of Indian Bank:**

 
 
• **Indian Bank** was established on **August 15, 1907**, as part of the **Swadeshi Movement** to promote indigenous enterprises.
 
• The bank is headquartered in **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**, and has a significant presence with thousands of branches and **ATMs** across **India** and international locations like **Singapore** and **Colombo**.
 
• On **April 1, 2020**, **Allahabad Bank** was merged into **Indian Bank**, making it the **seventh-largest** public sector bank in the country in terms of **business volume**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Year 2025 Vision:**
 
 
• The **2025** target for **‘Next LEAP’** coincides with the broader national goal of achieving a **$5 trillion economy**, where public sector banks play a pivotal role in **financial inclusion**.
 
• The bank aims to achieve a significant increase in its **Net Interest Margin (NIM)** and **Return on Assets (ROA)** by the end of the **2025** financial cycle through these HR reforms.
 
 
 
• **Digital Initiatives:**
 
 
• Apart from staff engagement, the bank has introduced **‘IndOASIS’**, a comprehensive **mobile banking application**, to provide seamless **digital banking** experiences to its customers.
 
• The bank is also focusing on **RAM (Retail, Agriculture, and MSME)** sectors to drive its credit growth and support the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiative.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **‘Next LEAP’** initiative is a response to the rapidly changing **banking landscape** in **India**, characterized by intense competition from **Private Banks** and **FinTech** companies.
 
• It emphasizes **talent management** and **succession planning**, ensuring that the bank has a steady pipeline of leaders to manage its growing **asset base**.
 
• By fostering a culture of **innovation** and **accountability**, **bank** intends to improve its **Asset Quality** and reduce **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)** through better-trained credit appraisal teams.

questions.question: In the 2025 Ludhiana West by-election, which party emerged victorious?

• The **Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)** successfully retained its political influence in the **Ludhiana West** constituency during the **2025 by-election**, following the trends established in the **2022 General Assembly Elections**.

questions.question: Which Indian political leader is known for the 'Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra' campaign in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shivraj Singh Chouhan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Viksit Bharat Sankalp Yatra** is a nationwide outreach initiative of the **Government of India** aimed at achieving **100% saturation** of flagship schemes across all **Gram Panchayats** and urban local bodies.
 
• **Shivraj Singh Chouhan**, as the **Union Minister of Rural Development** and **Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare** (appointed in **June 2024**), is a key leader responsible for the campaign's progress and rural outreach in **2024** and **2025**. ***Hence, this option is correct.***
 
• The Yatra was officially launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** on **November 15, 2023**, coinciding with **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas** from **Khunti, Jharkhand**.
 
• The primary function of the Yatra is to raise awareness and provide on-the-spot enrollment for welfare programs through specially designed **Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) vans**.
 
• Key schemes promoted during this campaign include **PM-Kisan**, **Ayushman Bharat**, **PM Ujjwala Yojana**, and **PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana**, ensuring that the benefits reach the **"last mile"** of the population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Viksit Bharat @2047:** This is a vision document and roadmap to transform India into a **developed nation** by the **100th year of Independence** in **2047**. The Yatra serves as a foundational step toward this long-term economic and social goal.
 
• **Janjatiya Gaurav Divas:** The campaign launch date, **November 15**, marks the birth anniversary of the legendary tribal leader **Birsa Munda**. This emphasizes the government's focus on **tribal development** and inclusion.
 
• **Scope and Data:** The Yatra targets coverage of over **2.6 lakh Gram Panchayats** and approximately **4,000 urban local bodies**, making it one of the largest ever government-to-citizen outreach programs in the country.
 
• **Digital Integration:** The campaign tracks real-time progress through a dedicated **portal and mobile app**, capturing data on the number of beneficiaries reached and testimonies (**"Meri Kahani Meri Zubani"**) shared by citizens.
 
• **Role of Government Departments:** Various ministries, including the **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting** and the **Ministry of Rural Development**, collaborate to manage the logistics of the **mobile vans** and community interaction sessions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rahul Gandhi:** He is a senior leader of the **Indian National Congress** known for leading the **Bharat Jodo Yatra** (2022–2023) and the **Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra** (2024), which were opposition-led political marches. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Mallikarjun Kharge:** He currently serves as the **President of the Indian National Congress** and the **Leader of the Opposition** in the **Rajya Sabha**. His role is primarily focused on parliamentary and party leadership rather than government-led outreach campaigns like Viksit Bharat. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Yogi Adityanath:** He is the **Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh**. While he has been instrumental in implementing the Yatra within **Uttar Pradesh**, he is not the national leader identified with the broader **2025** central ministerial oversight of the campaign. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Target Beneficiaries:** The campaign specifically focuses on **women**, **farmers**, **youth**, and the **economically marginalized (Gareeb)**, often referred to as the **"four pillars"** of a developed India by the current administration.

7f

questions.question: Which city was declared India’s 'Leopard Capital' on 5 June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Bengaluru__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On 5 June 2025, Bengaluru was named India’s "Leopard Capital" following a comprehensive year-long camera-trap survey.
 
• The city earned this title by recording the highest number of free-ranging wild leopards among all Indian metropolitan cities, surpassing Mumbai.
 
• Estimated Population: The survey, conducted by the Holématthi Nature Foundation (HNF) and led by conservationist Dr. Sanjay Gubbi, estimated 80–85 leopards in the forests and scrublands surrounding the city.
 
• Surpassing Mumbai: Bengaluru overtook Mumbai's previous record of approximately 54 leopards in Sanjay Gandhi National Park.
 
• Bannerghatta Contribution: A significant portion of the population—54 individuals—was recorded within Bannerghatta National Park, with roughly 30 more found in fringe forest patches like Turahalli and Roerich Estate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Leopard (Rajasthan):**

 
 
• **Rajasthan** became the first state in India to launch a dedicated **Project Leopard** in **2017**.
 
• The project focuses on **habitat conservation**, **prey base management**, and mitigating **man-animal conflict** across **eight** identified sanctuaries.
 
• Other major leopard habitats in the state include **Jhalana Leopard Reserve** in **Jaipur** and the **Jawai** region in **Pali**.
 
 
 
• **Leopard Characteristics and Features:**
 
 
• The leopard (**Panthera pardus**) is the smallest of the **big cats** but is known for its extreme **agility** and **nocturnal** hunting habits.
 
• They are highly **adaptable** and can survive in diverse climates, ranging from **tropical rainforests** to **arid rocky terrains** like the **Aravalli Range**.
 
• Leopards are **solitary** animals, and their **rosettes** (spots) serve as excellent camouflage in the scrub forests of **Rajasthan**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Context:**
 
 
• The **Aravalli Hills** are among the world's oldest **fold mountains**, stretching across **Gujarat**, **Rajasthan**, and **Haryana**.
 
• The **rocky outcrops** and **cave systems** in the **Udaipur** segment of the Aravallis provide natural shelters for leopards, making it a **prime location** for their survival.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conservation Status:**

 
 
• Leopards are protected under **Schedule I** of the Indian **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, granting them the highest level of legal protection in the **country**.
 
• On the **IUCN Red List** of Threatened Species, the leopard is categorized as **Vulnerable** due to habitat loss and **illegal wildlife trade**.
 
 
 
• **Population Data:**

questions.question: In February 2025, in which district did the NDRF launch an avalanche rescue operation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chamoli**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** launched a major rescue operation in the **Chamoli** district of **Uttarakhand** following a significant avalanche in the high-altitude regions.
 
• The rescue operation was necessitated by heavy snowfall and sudden temperature variations that led to snow instability in the **Dhauliganga** and **Rishiganga** river valleys. **Chamoli** is a high-risk zone for such geological and climatic events. *Hence, the statement regarding the location being Chamoli is correct.*
 
• The **NDRF** worked in close coordination with the **State Disaster Response Force (SDRF)** and the **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP)** to locate individuals stranded in remote trekking routes and border villages. 
 
• The operation utilized advanced equipment, including **thermal sensors** and **snow-probes**, to identify life beneath the snow layers. This highlights the **technical capabilities** of the **NDRF** in specialized mountain rescues.
 
• The **Chamoli** district is strategically and ecologically sensitive, housing major pilgrimage sites like **Badrinath** and **Hemkund Sahib**, making rapid response by central agencies like the **NDRF** crucial for safety and infrastructure protection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF):**
 
 
• The **NDRF** was established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**. It is a specialized force constituted for the purpose of a specialist response to a threatening disaster situation or disaster.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and currently consists of **16 battalions** (as of 2024-25) stationed across the country to ensure a quick response to various types of calamities, including **earthquakes**, **floods**, and **CBRN** (Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear) emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Chamoli District:**
 
 
• **Chamoli** is the second-largest district of **Uttarakhand** and is located in the **Central Himalayas**. It is bounded by **Tibet** to the north.
 
• The region is characterized by steep slopes and narrow valleys, making it highly susceptible to **Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs)** and **landslides**. Notable past events include the **2021 Rishi Ganga disaster**.
 
 
 
• **Avalanche Causes and Monitoring:**
 
 
• Avalanches in the **Himalayan** region are often triggered by the accumulation of heavy snow on slopes exceeding **30-45 degrees**.
 
• The **Defence Geo-Informatics Research Establishment (DGRE)**, formerly known as **SASE**, is the primary body responsible for monitoring and issuing **avalanche warnings** in the mountainous terrains of **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Impact:** Increased frequency of avalanches in **February** is often linked to **climate change**, which causes erratic **Western Disturbances** and rapid melting-refreezing cycles of Himalayan glaciers.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, headed by the **Prime Minister**, provides the policy framework, while the **NDRF** acts as the executive force on the ground.
 
• **Uttarkashi vs. Chamoli:** While **Uttarkashi** also experienced an avalanche in recent years (notably the **2022 Draupadi ka Danda** incident), the specific rescue operation mentioned for **February 2025** identifies **Chamoli** as the primary zone of deployment.
</ul

questions.question: In August 2025, the report ‘Unlocking a $200 Billion Opportunity: Electric Vehicles in India,’ assessing challenges and key steps for India’s Electric Mobility transition, was released by ________.

• The report titled ‘**Unlocking a $200 Billion Opportunity: Electric Vehicles in India**’ was released by **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) in **August 2025** to provide a roadmap for the country’s transition toward **Electric Mobility**.
 
• This comprehensive study was developed in collaboration with **RMI** (Rocky Mountain Institute) and **RMI India** to assess the capital requirements and financing challenges in the **Electric Vehicle (EV)** sector.
 
• The report highlights that India requires a cumulative investment of **$200 billion** (approximately **Rs 14.37 lakh crore**) by the **year 2030** to achieve its targets for vehicle production, **charging infrastructure**, and battery manufacturing.
 
• It identifies that the **transition to electric vehicles** is not just an environmental necessity but a massive economic opportunity that can reduce **oil imports** and position India as a global manufacturing hub.
 
• The primary focus of the report is on **mobilizing private capital** and identifying the **financing gap** that exists for retail **EV loans**, which is crucial for the **2-wheeler** and **3-wheeler** segments. *Hence, the statement regarding NITI Aayog being the releasing authority is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FAME-II Scheme**: The **Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles** (FAME) India Phase II was launched by the **Ministry of Heavy Industries** with a significant **budgetary outlay** to subsidize **EV purchases** and support **charging stations**.
 
• **PLI Scheme for ACC**: The **Government of India** introduced a **Production Linked Incentive (PLI)** scheme for **Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC)** battery storage with an investment of **Rs 18,100 crore** to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce dependency on **imports**.
 
• **2030 EV Ambition**: India aims to achieve **30%** electric vehicle penetration for **private cars**, **70%** for **commercial vehicles**, and **80%** for **two and three-wheelers** by the **year 2030**.
 
• **e-AMRIT Portal**: **NITI Aayog** launched the **e-AMRIT** (Accelerated e-Mobility Revolution for India’s Transportation) web portal during the **COP26 summit** to serve as a **one-stop-shop** for all information regarding **electric vehicles** in **India**.
 
• **GST Benefits**: To encourage **consumers**, the **GST Council** reduced the tax rate on **Electric Vehicles** from **12%** to **5%**, and on **chargers/charging stations** from **18%** to **5%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)**: One of the key recommendations in such **NITI Aayog** reports is the inclusion of **Electric Vehicles** under the **Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI)** **Priority Sector Lending** guidelines to ensure **low-cost financing**.
 
• **Economic Impact**: Achieving the **$200 billion** investment target is estimated to reduce **carbon dioxide emissions** significantly and save billions in **foreign exchange** by reducing **crude oil** demand.
 
• **Infrastructure Requirements**: The report emphasizes that **India** will need approximately **2.9 million** public **charging points** by **2030** to support the projected growth of the **EV fleet**.
 
• **State-Level Policies**: Various **States** like **Delhi**, **Maharashtra**, and **Karnataka** have released their own **EV policies** providing **road tax exemptions** and **registration fee waivers** to supplement **Central Government** efforts.
</ul

questions.question: Who chaired the 10th Governing Council Meeting of the NITI Aayog on 24 May 2025?

__
 
• The **Governing Council** of **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) is chaired by the **Prime Minister of India**, who serves as its **Ex-officio Chairperson**. As of the year **2025**, **Shri Narendra Modi** holds this position and thus chaired the **10th Governing Council Meeting** on **24 May 2025**. ***Hence, statement C is correct.***
 
• The meeting focuses on the **National Development Agenda**, involving a shared vision between the **Center and the States** to foster **Cooperative Federalism**.
 
• The **Governing Council** comprises the **Prime Minister**, **Chief Ministers** of all States and Union Territories with Legislatures, and **Lieutenant Governors** of other Union Territories.
 
• Key agendas for the **10th meeting** typically revolve around the roadmap for **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**, emphasizing **economic growth**, **social welfare**, and **infrastructure development**.
 
• **Amit Shah**, **Manohar Lal Khattar**, and **JP Nadda** are high-ranking **Union Ministers** who serve as **Ex-officio members** or **Special Invitees** but do not hold the authority to chair the Governing Council meeting when the Prime Minister is present. ***Hence, statements A, B, and D are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog Establishment:** It was established on **January 1, 2015**, by a resolution of the Union Cabinet. It replaced the **Planning Commission**, which had been in existence since **1950**. Unlike the Planning Commission, which followed a top-down approach, **NITI Aayog** follows a **bottom-up approach**.
 
• **Organizational Structure:** The hierarchy includes a **Vice-Chairperson** (appointed by the PM), a **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**, **Full-time Members**, **Ex-officio Members** (maximum 4 from the Union Council of Ministers), and **Special Invitees**.
 
• **Hubs of NITI Aayog:** It operates through two main hubs: the **Team India Hub** (carrying the interface of States with the Center) and the **Knowledge and Innovation Hub** (building the think-tank capacity).
 
• **Reports and Indices:** **NITI Aayog** is responsible for publishing several important indices, such as the **SDG India Index**, **Composite Water Management Index**, **School Education Quality Index**, and the **India Innovation Index**.
 
• **Cooperative Federalism:** One of the primary mandates is to recognize that **strong States make a strong Nation**. It provides a platform to resolve inter-sectoral and inter-departmental issues to accelerate the **development agenda**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Prime Minister:** As the **Chairperson**, the **PM** sets the tone for national priorities. The **Governing Council** meetings are the highest decision-making platform in the organization.
 
• **Membership Nuances:** **Amit Shah** serves as the **Union Minister of Home Affairs**, while **JP Nadda** serves as the **Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare**. Both are **Ex-officio members** of **NITI Aayog** as of **2024-2025**.
 
• **Administrative Location:** The headquarters of **NITI Aayog** is located at **Yojana Bhawan**, **Sansad Marg**, **New Delhi**.
 
• **Policy Functions:** The organization performs **Strategic and Long-term Policy** and program frameworks, and monitors their progress through **data-driven governance**.
</ul

• **Giorgio Armani** was a legendary and highly influential **Italian** fashion designer, widely regarded as one of the most successful designers to emerge from **Europe**.
 
• He was born on **July 11, 1934**, in the city of **Piacenza**, located in the **Emilia-Romagna** region of **Northern Italy**.
 
• After initially studying **medicine** at the **University of Milan** and serving in the **military**, he transitioned into the fashion industry, starting as a window dresser at **La Rinascente**, a famous department store in **Milan**.
 
• In **1975**, along with his business partner **Sergio Galeotti**, he founded **Giorgio Armani S.p.A.** in **Milan**, which grew to become a global luxury powerhouse.
 
• He became globally famous for his **unstructured jackets** and **minimalist** designs, which revolutionized **menswear** and **womenswear** by introducing a more relaxed yet elegant **Italian** aesthetic.
 
• Armani's international breakthrough occurred in **1980** when he designed the wardrobe for **Richard Gere** in the film **American Gigolo**, establishing the "Armani look" as a symbol of **sophistication** and **power**.

__
 
• **Brand Portfolio and Diversification:** The Armani empire encompasses a wide range of sub-brands including **Giorgio Armani** (signature line), **Emporio Armani** (targeted at a younger demographic), **Armani Exchange (A|X)** (mass-market urban style), and **Armani Privé** (high-end couture).
 
• **Global Expansion:** By the **1990s** and **2000s**, the brand expanded into numerous industries including **cosmetics**, **eyewear**, **watches**, and **home interiors** through the **Armani/Casa** line.
 
• **Hospitality Industry:** Armani ventured into luxury hospitality with the opening of the **Armani Hotel** in the **Burj Khalifa**, **Dubai**, in **2010**, and a second flagship hotel in **Milan** in **2011**.
 
• **Economic Powerhouse:** Giorgio Armani remains one of the few major **Italian** fashion houses to remain **independent**, resisting acquisition by major luxury conglomerates like **LVMH** or **Kering**.
 
• **Sports and Cultural Impact:** He has a significant presence in sports, notably as the owner of the **Olimpia Milano** basketball team and the designer of the **Italian Olympic** team's parade uniforms for multiple **Olympic Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ethical Leadership:** In **2006**, Armani was the first major designer to ban models with a **body mass index (BMI)** under **18** following the death of a model due to anorexia-related complications.
 
• **Sustainability:** In **2016**, the **Armani Group** committed to going **fur-free** across all its labels, highlighting a significant shift toward **animal welfare** in the luxury fashion sector.
 
• **Honors and Awards:** He was honored with the **Knight Grand Cross of the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic** in **2021**, the highest civil honor in **Italy**, for his contribution to **Italian** culture and economy.
 
• **Legacy:** Often called "King Giorgio," his legacy is defined by the **neutral color palettes** (especially **greige**) and the "power suit" that empowered women in the workforce during the **1980s** and **1990s**.

questions.question: Which legendary sprinter was named a Guinness World Records ICON in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Usain Bolt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Usain Bolt**, the **Jamaican** sprinting legend, was named a **Guinness World Records ICON** in **June 2025** (marking a milestone anniversary of his peak achievements) for his unprecedented dominance and lasting impact on **Track and Field**. *Hence, option B is correct.*
 
• He is the world record holder in the **100 metres**, **200 metres**, and the **4 × 100 metres relay**, making him the **fastest man in history**. His 100m record of **9.58 seconds** and 200m record of **19.19 seconds** were both set at the **2009 World Athletics Championships** in **Berlin**, **Germany**.
 
• **Usain Bolt** has secured a total of **8 Olympic gold medals** and is the only sprinter to win the **Olympic 100m and 200m titles** at three consecutive **Olympics** (**Beijing 2008**, **London 2012**, and **Rio 2016**).
 
• The title of **Guinness World Records ICON** is reserved for individuals whose achievements are so significant that they redefine their field; Bolt holds the record for the **most IAAF World Championship gold medals** won by a male athlete (**11 gold medals**).
 
• Other athletes mentioned like **Justin Gatlin**, **Carl Lewis**, and **Michael Johnson** are legends in their own right, but they do not hold the specific **ICON** status designated for this timeframe or the current world records in the primary sprint categories. *Hence, options A, C, and D are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Guinness World Records (GWR):** Originally known as the **Guinness Book of Records**, it was first published in **1955** by the **Guinness Brewery**. It serves as the primary international authority on **record-breaking achievements** across human and natural categories.
 
• **Justin Gatlin:** An **American** sprinter who was a major rival to Bolt. He won the **Olympic 100m gold** in **2004** and the **World Championship gold** in **2005** and **2017**. He is known for his longevity in the sport, competing well into his late **30s**.
 
• **Carl Lewis:** A former **American** track and field athlete who won **9 Olympic gold medals** and **8 World Championship gold medals**. He dominated the **100m**, **200m**, and **Long Jump** during the **1980s** and **1990s**.
 
• **Michael Johnson:** An **American** sprinter who specialized in the **200m** and **400m**. He held the 200m world record of **19.32 seconds** (set at the **1996 Atlanta Olympics**) for **12 years** until it was broken by **Usain Bolt** in **2008**.
 
• **Sprinting Physics:** During his 100m record run in **2009**, Bolt reached a **top speed** of **44.72 km/h** (**27.78 mph**), which remains the highest speed ever recorded for a human being on foot.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Berlin Breakthrough:** The **year 2009** remains the most significant in sprinting history, as the **100m** and **200m** world records were lowered by the largest margins since the introduction of **electronic timing**.
 
• **Retirement:** **Usain Bolt** officially retired from athletics after the **2017 World Championships** held in **London**. Following his track career, he briefly explored **professional football** in **Australia** and **Europe**.
 
• **Linguistic and Cultural Impact:** Bolt’s signature **"To Di World"** pose (often called the **lightning bolt**) became a global symbol of **victory** and **excellence**, contributing to his **ICON** status.
 
• **World Athletics:** Formerly known as the **IAAF** (International Association of Athletics Federations), it is the **international governing body** for the sport of **athletics**, which ratifies all sprint world records.

questions.question: The inaugural Everest Climbers’ Summit focused on climate, held in 2025, took place in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathmandu, Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **inaugural Everest Climbers’ Summit** on climate change was held in **Kathmandu, Nepal**, in **May 2025**. The summit was organized to bring together world-renowned mountaineers to highlight the alarming rate of **glacier melt** in the **Himalayas**.
 
• The event was timed to coincide with the **International Year of Glaciers' Preservation** (**2025**), as declared by the **United Nations General Assembly**. This initiative seeks to raise global awareness about the vulnerability of mountain ecosystems.
 
• The summit served as a platform for climbers who have summited **Mount Everest** multiple times to share their **firsthand observations** of environmental changes, such as the thinning of the **Khumbu Glacier** and the increasing frequency of **avalanches**.
 
• A key objective of the **2025 Summit** in **Kathmandu** was to pressure the international community to meet the goals of the **Paris Agreement**, specifically aiming to limit global warming to **1.5°C** to save the "**Water Tower of Asia**."
 
• The **Government of Nepal**, through the **Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation**, led the initiative to ensure that the voices of those who know the mountains best are heard in global climate policy discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mount Everest (Sagarmatha):** It is the highest peak in the world, with an official elevation of **8,848.86 meters**. It is located in the **Mahalangur Himal** sub-range of the **Himalayas**, straddling the border between **Nepal** and **China** (Tibet).
 
• **Climate Impact on the Third Pole:** The **Himalayan-Hindu Kush** region is often referred to as the **Third Pole** because it contains the largest ice reserves outside the polar regions. Recent data from **ICIMOD** (International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development) suggests that glaciers in this region could lose **30% to 80%** of their volume by the year **2100**.
 
• **The Khumbu Glacier:** This is the highest glacier in the world, located in the **Solukhumbu District** of **Nepal**. Studies have shown that the **South Col Glacier** on Everest has lost nearly **2 meters** of ice thickness annually in recent decades due to **anthropogenic climate change**.
 
• **Sagarmatha Sambaad:** This is a multi-stakeholder dialogue forum established by the **Government of Nepal** in **2019**. It focuses on global, regional, and national issues, with **climate change** being a primary theme for its inaugural sessions.
 
• **Historical Significance:** The summit also paid tribute to the **72nd anniversary** of the first successful ascent of **Mount Everest** by **Sir Edmund Hillary** and **Tenzing Norgay** in **1953**, emphasizing that the mountain they climbed is vastly different from the one climbers face today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical Facts:** **Kathmandu** is the capital of **Nepal** and sits at an altitude of approximately **1,400 meters**. It is the primary logistics base for almost all **Everest expeditions**.
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact:** More than **1.65 billion people** depend on the **ten major rivers** that originate in the **Hindu Kush Himalaya** region for water, agriculture, and energy. Any disruption in glacier stability threatens the **food and water security** of **South Asia**.
 
• **International Year of Glaciers' Preservation:** In **2022**, the **UN** passed a resolution, sponsored by **Tajikistan** and supported by **Nepal**, to declare **2025** as a year to focus on **glacier retreat** and its consequences for **sea-level rise** and **biodiversity**.
 
• **Everest Cleanup Campaigns:** Parallel to climate summits, **Nepal** regularly conducts "**Mountain Clean-up Campaigns**" led by the **Nepalese Army** to remove tonnes of waste and **microplastics** from high-altitude camps, highlighting the **pollution** aspect of environmental degradation.
